compound.name: (+)-pulegone
compound.one_liner: Peppermint oil ketone limited to ≤3 % by Ph. Eur.; hepatotoxic via bioactivation, with an EMA combined limit.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Mentha x piperita L., folium and aetheroleum, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/522409/2013 (15 Jan 2020). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/assessment-report-mentha-x-piperita-l-folium-and-aetheroleum-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: PULEGONE Leaf 0-440 ppm. KNApSAcK: Pulegone C00000827 in Mentha piperita. | Basis as recorded: % of essential oil (Ph. Eur. limit)

pharmacology.mechanism: Bioactivation of pulegone, with menthofuran as a major metabolite, is a prerequisite for its hepatotoxicity [3].

evidence.claim: Pulegone is toxic to liver and kidney in rats.
evidence.test_article_detail: pulegone, NTP 3-month rat study (as summarised by EMA)
evidence.outcome_summary: NOAEL 37.5 mg/kg bw/day; basis of the EMA limit.

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

safety_flags.detail: Ph. Eur. limits pulegone to ≤3 % of peppermint oil [6].
safety_flags.threshold_or_limit: pulegone + menthofuran 0.75 mg/kg bw/day (37.5 mg/person/day) lifelong; 75 mg/day for use under 1 year
safety_flags.source_citation: EMA/HMPC public statement on pulegone and menthofuran, EMA/HMPC/138386/2005 Rev.1 (2016)

compound.teaching_note: In peppermint, pulegone is kept low by pharmacopoeial specification (≤3 % of oil) [6].
gaps: No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
